thread:
Maya: Hey all — we need a quick sync on the new GPU pool metrics for Hosted + Dedicated. primary asks: SM occupancy, per-host GPU memory used, and queue depth.
Josh: +1. goal is to have a single source of truth for console dashboards and routing rules.
Priya: FYI SRE: sampling cadence/ingest cost matters. 1s is expensive at scale. proposing 10s for occupancy, 30s for memory, event-driven for queue depth (on change). thoughts?
Maya: 10s for SM occupancy seems fine for visibility. queue depth needs near-real-time for routing decisions — prefer <5s.
Oliver: Console UX: we want a heatmap by pool -> host -> SM occupancy percentile. also a per-tenant view for Dedicated (tenant_id tag). Make sure tags exist in the telemetry payload.
Sam: Metric names suggestion: `gpu.sm_occupancy_pct`, `gpu.gmem_used_mb`, `gpu.sm_queue_depth`. add tags: pool:(hosted|dedicated), host_id, gpu_index, model_family, tenant_id (optional).
Josh: Agree on names. contract note: do not include batch-level payloads to keep size small. one metric line per sample.
Priya: Alerts/thresholds proposal for SLOs: hosted warning when occupancy > 80% for 5m, critical > 92% for 1m; dedicated warning > 88% for 5m, critical > 97% for 1m. queue depth alert when depth > 12 sustained 30s (hosted) or > 20 (dedicated).
Taylor: From product/console POV: alerts should map to routing suggestions in the UI: e.g., recommended model-variant fallback or suggest spilling to Dedicated. show cost delta estimate when recommending fallback.
Maya: routing policy integration: runtime needs a simple API that returns pool health: `GET /v1/pools/{pool}/health?agg=cluster` with fields (occupancy_pct, avg_queue, headroom_pct). keep it small and cacheable (5s).
Josh: API shape ok, but we need to decide owner for the health endpoint — eng-runtime will implement, but eng-platform owns telemetry ingestion and aggregation. recommend eng-platform serves the aggregated endpoint.
Maya: ok runtime will call eng-platform endpoint for routing. we’ll add local fallback logic if endpoint times out.
Oliver: Dashboard panels: 1) cluster heatmap (pool level) 2) top-ten hosts by occupancy 3) per-dedicated-tenant page 4) small inline routing simulator (input occupancy/queue -> recommended action).
Priya: Telemetry constraints: include `sample_ts`, `pool`, `host_id`, `gpu_index`, `value`, `metric_name`. prefer protobuf or compressed JSON over wire. storage retention: keep 30d at 10s resolution for dashboards, aggregated hourly for 90d.
Sam: ML note: attach `model_family` tag so we can correlate heavy models with memory spikes.
Josh: Owners and rollout: eng-platform -> telemetry pipeline + aggregation (owner: Josh), eng-runtime -> runtime callers + local fallback (owner: Maya), console panels (owner: Oliver), alerts & SLOs (owner: Priya), product UX (Taylor), ML tagging (Sam).
Maya: Rollout plan: 1) implement schema + staging pipeline (48h smoke), 2) enable metrics for Hosted staging clusters, 3) 5% traffic canary for routing calls -> monitor false positives for 72h, 4) full rollout.
Priya: Can we add a dashboard for ingress cost so infra knows billing impact during canary? keep a meter for events/sec and bytes/sec.
Josh: Good call. add `telemetry.events_per_min` and `telemetry.bytes_per_min` aggregated.
infra-bot: deploy-notice: telemetry-pipeline v0.3 will deploy to staging at 2026-03-22T03:00Z.
Oliver: UX followups — I’ll wireframe heatmap and routing simulator by EOD Friday and post screenshots here.
Maya: Next steps: Josh create telemetry contract PR with schema + example payload; Sam add model_family tagging to inference service; Priya create alert docs with thresholds; Oliver make wireframes. We’ll reconvene after PR review.
Josh: I’ll put the PR up today: https://git.internal/r/redwood/telemetry/pulls/182 
Taylor: Thanks everyone — this should make dedicated capacity and routing much more predictable. :thumbsup:
Maya: Cheers.
